newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta sees good office space demand - report.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta sees good office space demand - report.

text.p: Jakarta is experiencing a vigorous demand for office space with substantial leases by local and foreign companies in the banking, financial services and pharmaceutical sectors, property consultants Colliers Jardine said on Thursday.

PT Colliers Jardine Indonesia said in a news release on its half-yearly review of Asia Pacific property trends that net demand for additional office space during the first half of 1996 was around 120,000 sq metres.

"Pre-commitments averaging 60 percent of planned space are being achieved for premium buildings under construction and those scheduled for completion in the short term," Managing Director Peter Collins said.
He said the strength of leasing activity was partly fuelled by large-scale users taking advantage of a low rental climate to relocate to newer premises.
He expected rents to show a downward trend in the long term.
Supply of new floor space in the first six months of the year was over 100,000 sq metres, compared to around 125,000 sq metres in the same 1995 period.
"Additional new floor space supply of 363,516 sq metres is expected to become available over the remainder of the year," Collins said.
But he said some projects could be delayed due to high interest rates and a squeeze on property lending.

He said the property investment market in Jakarta had been subdued recently and he expected capital values of offices in the prime central business district area to decrease slightly in the near term due to an anticipated surge in supply.
The report said demand for commercial space in Indonesia's second city, Surabaya, remained "torpid" with only 3,000 sq metres of floor area taken up in the first half of the year.
International retailers entering the Jakarta market through franchise agreements continued to rise, and most retail centres being completed this year were already 90 percent leased.
"Achieved rentals should stay steady in the year ahead," Collins said.
In the industrial sector, the report said, enquiries from foreign investors seeking industrial poremises in Jakarta had cooled compared to 1995, but domestic manufacturers were still active.
